prompt: You're building the first prototype of an email summarizer this week. You have no labeled data yet.
why: Start with clear instructions and a couple of examples in the prompt; it's the fastest lever.
trap: Fine-tuning needs data you don't have and slows iteration.

prompt: The model's summaries are too long and miss action items. Adding three good examples to the prompt might be enough.
tells: Adding three good examples to the prompt
why: Few-shot examples and explicit instructions often fix format and focus immediately.
trap: Don't reach for training when a prompt change hasn't been tried.

prompt: On multi-step math word problems the model often jumps to wrong answers. You want it to work through the steps before answering, without any training.
tells: work through the steps before answering
why: Ask for step-by-step reasoning (or enable extended thinking) before the final answer.
trap: A bigger model might help, but the cheapest fix is asking it to reason first.

prompt: Answers are generic because the model doesn't know the user is a beginner nurse. You can include that in every request.
tells: doesn't know the user is a beginner nurse
why: Give the audience and context in the system prompt.
trap: Retrieval is for facts from documents, not for describing who you're talking to.

prompt: A chatbot's replies sound stiff and corporate. You'd like a friendly, casual tone, and you can change the prompt today.
why: Describe the tone and show an example in the system prompt; it's the fastest lever.
trap: Try the prompt before training anything.

prompt: Asked to "clean up" user notes, the model sometimes rewrites meaning, sometimes only fixes typos. The instructions are a single vague line.
why: Spell out exactly what to change and what to keep; ambiguity in, variance out.
trap: Evals will measure the inconsistency, but the fix is clearer instructions.

prompt: When users paste text containing "Summary:" lines, the model confuses their text with your instructions.
tells: confuses their text with your instructions
why: Wrap user content in clear delimiters (e.g. XML tags) and refer to it by name.
trap: Not an attack, just unclear boundaries in the prompt.

prompt: One giant prompt asks the model to extract entities, classify sentiment and draft a reply all at once, and each part is mediocre.
why: Split into a chain of focused prompts, each doing one job well.
trap: A bigger model might mask it; smaller steps fix it.
